turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Mr. Hale." *(She doesn't sit.)* "You asked for this meeting, so I'll start with a question. Why did my son find out about a zero from an online gradebook, in the middle of class, and not from a phone call to me?"

"I have a call at 4:40. Go ahead."

"Okay."

*(She sets her bag on the nearest desk and stays standing.)*

"Finish. I'll want the dates in an email afterward."
I have 140 students. I don't have time to be cross-examined by every parent with a law degree.

"I asked one question, Mr. Hale. You haven't answered it."

*(A beat.)*

"'Cross-examined.' Is that what this is? Because I came to listen. You asked for the meeting. So tell me what you have, and when you got it."

"And I'd like to know when you decided on the zero. Before you spoke to Owen, or after?"
You don't get to talk to me like I'm on the stand.

"Fine."

*(She pulls out the nearest student chair and sits, bag on her knee.)*

"No stand. I'm Owen's mother, and I'm sitting down. You don't want to be asked questions, so I'll make it simple. Tell me what happened, in order, starting with the day you read the essay."

"I'll listen. I won't interrupt." *(She glances at her watch.)* "But I'll want to know who decided on the zero, and whether Owen was asked anything first."
